trust_decision.summary: Untrusted e-mail body text is parsed into reported URLs/domains; the decision 'is this URL/domain reportable' is made in two separate places: clean_found_uri (entity decode + host validation, which the report's examples reach) and the dom_regex pass over the raw body slice in parse_email that builds the 'domain'/'domain_hash' output and which clean_found_uri never calls.

landing_point.why: The summary says URLs escaped as HTML entities bypass extraction; the first place an engineer looks is clean_found_uri, where an unescape call already exists at eml_parser/parser.py:784-785 but runs after the dot gate at :751 and after URL parse/host validation at :756-772, so an entity-escaped URL is dropped or validated on the escaped host.

fix_sites.module_kind: public library API method in eml_parser.parser

fix_sites.entry_point: EmlParser.decode_email_bytes / decode_email -> parse_email, producing the body 'domain' / 'domain_hash' field

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The URL patterns require a literal scheme separator, so an entity-escaped scheme does not look like a URL to any extractor; HTML entities are an HTML-attribute concern and every href/src already goes through the dedicated href regex, so a scheme-escaped string in a text/plain part can be argued to be a regex limitation rather than the reported bypass.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The body string and its sha256 must stay the raw source text: unescaping has to happen per extracted URL, not on the body before it is stored/hashed, or 'content' and 'hash' change (tests/test_emlparser.py:405 asserts an exact body hash) while returned URLs must still have '&' decoded to '&' (tests/test_emlparser.py:122).

O6_input_shapes: fully escaped URL in an href attribute: scheme separators and dots as decimal references (https://host.tld/path)
partially escaped URL: literal scheme with escaped dots in the host
named entity & inside a query string
entity-escaped mailto: value (mailto:user@host.tld) reported as a scheme-less URL
escaped host in an unquoted img src attribute (other.example.com?something&blub)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A URL whose scheme/www separator is entity-escaped (https://evil.com or www.evil.com) in a text/plain part matches neither url_regex_www nor url_regex_simple, so it never reaches clean_found_uri; the published fix leaves both regexes untouched.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: HTML entities only occur in HTML parts and HTML href/src values already take the href regex, so plain-text with an escaped scheme is a regex limitation, not the reported HTML-attribute bypass.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: one file away from the landing point in the same package (regexes.py -> parser.py:471-476); the fix must also change get_uri_ondata's input

O8_uncovered_routes.route: An entity-escaped domain that is not inside a recognised URL (plain text evil.com) is still absent from the 'domain'/'domain_hash' output: dom_regex on the raw body slice cannot see escaped dots and the new URL-derived re-scan only looks at strings the URL regexes already matched.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: A bare escaped domain is not a URL, so it is outside an advisory about URL extraction; the domain field is a by-product of URL/body regex hits.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same function/loop as the second fix site; no code distance

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A get_domain_ondata / get_email_ondata helper mirroring get_uri_ondata, scanning a body slice with its own regex and needing the same entity normalisation
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The project already factors URL searching into a helper (get_uri_ondata) while e-mail/domain/IP scanning is inline in the same loop; a maintainer refactoring one of those passes into a helper would reproduce the pattern.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A clean_found_domain / normalise_host sibling of clean_found_uri used by the Received-header path in eml_parser/routing.py:51-60
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: routing.get_domain_ip already runs dom_regex over header text with no entity handling; adding host normalisation there alongside clean_found_uri is a natural next commit.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A separate URL/domain scan inside traverse_multipart / prepare_multipart_part_attachment for HTML attachments, bypassing the body loop
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The code explicitly treats .htm/.html attachments as body because they must not escape the URL scan; a maintainer could instead add an attachment-side scan with its own decode step.

O9_family: Improper encoding/escaping handling in URL extraction (CWE-116) - HTML-entity-escaped URLs and hosts bypass URL and domain extraction
